dct_description_sm:
The 2022 IPS identifies the Indigenous identity population as anyone who self-reported being at least one of the following:

  • an Indigenous person, that is, First Nations (North American Indian), Métis or Inuk (Inuit)
  • a Status Indian, that is, a Registered or Treaty Indian as defined by the Indian Act of Canada
  • a member of a First Nation or Indian band.

A person may have reported more than one Indigenous identity; for example, a respondent could have self-identified as both First Nations and Métis. For the 2022 IPS Public Use Microdata File (PUMF), persons who reported more than one Indigenous identity group are aggregated into one group called “Multiple Indigenous identities”.

The 2022 Indigenous Peoples Survey (IPS) is a national survey on the social and economic conditions of First Nations people living off reserve, Métis and Inuit, aged 1 year and over as of April 27, 2022. The objectives of the IPS are to identify the needs of these Indigenous groups and to inform policy and programming activities aimed at improving the well-being of Indigenous peoples. The IPS aims to provide current and relevant data for a variety of stakeholders, including Indigenous organizations, communities, service providers, researchers, governments and the general public. Funding was provided by three federal departments: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada, Indigenous Services Canada, and Employment and Social Development Canada.
